unitTitle: General and Fundamental Principles of Organic Chemistry
syllabusTopics: Purification and qualitative/quantitative analysis of organic compounds
Important organic reactions: oxidation, reduction, addition, elimination
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9. Filled 2026-10-06 (Class 12 track); no Class-12 PYQ bank in-corpus, so the board row is NEB-style with no fabricated citation.

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Reactions follow electrons: inductive effect pushes/pulls through σ bonds by electronegativity (±I, distance-fading), resonance delocalises π electrons over conjugated frames (±R, long-range), hyperconjugation leaks σ(C–H) density into empty p orbitals (carbocation stability ladder). Purification (distillation, crystallisation, chromatography) and Lassaigne analysis open every investigation; substitution/elimination/addition/redox close it.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: −I order: NO₂ > CN > COOH > halogens > OH > C≡C  ·  +I: alkyl, (CH₃)₃C > (CH₃)₂CH > CH₃  ·  carbocation stability: 3° > 2° > 1° (hyperconjugation +I count)  ·  Lassaigne: Na fusion → CN⁻/S²⁻/X⁻ detected  ·  fission: homolytic → radicals · heterolytic → ions

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Inductive effect dies within ~3 bonds; resonance needs planar conjugated p systems; hyperconjugation needs α-hydrogens aligned with the empty orbital. Lassaigne needs complete fusion (volatile samples escape). Electrophiles attack electron-rich sites, nucleophiles electron-poor — map the polarity first.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Formic acid out-acids acetic (no +I methyl to blunt it); chloroacetic beats both (−I Cl). Tert-butyl cation's 9 hyperconjugative C–H structures explain Markovnikov's preference quantitatively. Phenol's −OH pumps +R into the ring (super-activated); −NO₂ drains it (−R, meta-directing).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Acidity order HCOOH > CH₃COOH > CH₃CH₂COOH: alkyl +I donates into the carboxylate, destabilising the anion progressively — longer chain, weaker acid. Same logic ranks amines' basicity (with solvation twists) and carbocation rearrangement destinations.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Effects compete and sometimes cancel (aniline's +R vs −I nitrogen: +R wins for direction, −I taxes basicity). Gas-phase orders flip in solution (solvation). Hyperconjugation is a model, not a bond — over-invoking it explains everything and therefore nothing.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From electronegativity differences: polar σ bonds shift electron density measurably (dipole moments, pKa trends) — induction quantified. Resonance energy from heats of hydrogenation (benzene ~150 kJ/mol below Kekulé prediction). Hyperconjugation from C–H/C–C rotational barriers and the 3°>2°>1° rate ladder in SN1 solvolysis.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Acid/base ranking: count −I/+I groups near the centre, check resonance of the conjugate, then hyperconjugation. Reaction type? Find the electron move: pair splits uneven → ions (electrophile/nucleophile); even → radicals. Purification: bp gap → distillation; solubility gap → crystallisation.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: ±I/±R orders with acidity/basicity rankings; Lassaigne N/S/X detection steps; homolytic vs heterolytic fission with species matching; oxidation/reduction/addition/elimination classification drills.
